question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: 'The newly appointed director is responsible __ overseeing the regional operations.'

hint_ladder.title: Identify Idiomatic Expression
hint_ladder.text: The adjective 'responsible' takes different prepositions depending on context.

hint_ladder.title: Distinguish Targets
hint_ladder.text: Responsible TO a person/superior vs responsible FOR a task/duty.

hint_ladder.title: Check Target in Sentence
hint_ladder.text: 'Overseeing regional operations' is a task/duty.

hint_ladder.title: Select Preposition
hint_ladder.text: Tasks require 'responsible FOR'.

A.text: Correct! Responsible FOR is used with tasks or duties.

B.text: Incorrect idiom. Responsible with is not standard English.

C.text: Responsible TO is used when referring to a superior or authority (e.g. responsible to the Secretary).

D.text: Incorrect preposition choice.

next_time_rule: Use 'responsible FOR' with duties/tasks, and 'responsible TO' with authority figures.
blueprint_id: Prepositional Idioms — Responsible For vs Responsible To
deconstruct_text:
Idiomatic Preposition Rule:
- Responsible FOR + task/duty/action.
- Responsible TO + authority figure/person (e.g. responsible to the President).
Since 'overseeing operations' is a duty -> use 'responsible for'.

question_text: The auditor recommended that the municipal treasurer AMEND the financial report. What is the synonym for AMEND?

hint_ladder.title: Context Clue
hint_ladder.text: Recommending changes to a report before final submission.

hint_ladder.title: Root Meaning
hint_ladder.text: 'Amend' means to modify, revise, or alter for correctness.

hint_ladder.title: Evaluate Options
hint_ladder.text: To alter means to change or modify.

hint_ladder.title: Select Matching Option
hint_ladder.text: Option B is 'Alter'.

A.text: Discard means throw away, which is too destructive.

B.text: Correct! Alter means to modify or revise.

C.text: Approve means accept as is, opposite of amending.

D.text: Publish means release to public, independent of modifying.

next_time_rule: Amend means to alter, modify, or revise for accuracy.
blueprint_id: Vocabulary — Synonyms of Legal and Audit Terms
deconstruct_text:
Amend = to revise, alter, or change for improvement/correctness.
Synonym = Alter, Modify, Modify.

question_text: Identify the sentence that maintains parallel structure.

options.text: The new administrative officer likes organizing files, drafting letters, and to answer phone inquiries.
The new administrative officer likes organizing files, drafting letters, and answering phone inquiries.
The new administrative officer likes to organize files, drafting letters, and answering phone inquiries.
The new administrative officer likes file organization, drafting letters, and to answer phone inquiries.

hint_ladder.title: Identify List Items
hint_ladder.text: The sentence lists three duties: organizing, drafting, answering.

hint_ladder.title: Check Verb Forms
hint_ladder.text: All items in a list must use the same grammatical form (all gerunds -ing or all infinitives to...).

hint_ladder.title: Compare Sentence B
hint_ladder.text: Sentence B uses three gerunds: organizing, drafting, answering.

hint_ladder.title: Confirm Parallelism
hint_ladder.text: Sentence B is parallel because all listed actions end in -ing.

A.text: Breaks parallelism by mixing gerunds (organizing, drafting) with an infinitive (to answer).

B.text: Correct! Uses parallel gerund phrases (organizing, drafting, answering).

C.text: Breaks parallelism by starting with infinitive 'to organize' followed by gerunds.

D.text: Mixes noun phrase (file organization), gerund (drafting), and infinitive (to answer).

next_time_rule: Keep items in a series grammatically uniform (all -ing verbs or all to... infinitives).
blueprint_id: Parallel Structure — Parallel Gerund Phrases
deconstruct_text:
Parallelism requires items in a series to share identical grammatical structure.
Option B uses parallel gerunds: organizing, drafting, answering.
Option A mixes gerunds with infinitive 'to answer'.

question_text: Read the passage: 'Public accountability requires civil servants to perform duties with utmost integrity, efficiency, and dedication. Transparency in transactions ensures citizens maintain trust in government institutions.' What is the main idea of this statement?

options.text: Civil servants should receive higher salaries to maintain integrity.
Public trust relies on accountable and transparent government service.
Government transactions must be kept confidential to avoid public scrutiny.
Efficiency is more important than integrity in public administration.

hint_ladder.title: Focus on Core Concept
hint_ladder.text: Look at the two key words in the passage: accountability and transparency.

hint_ladder.title: Connect Core Concepts to Outcome
hint_ladder.text: Accountability + transparency lead to public trust.

hint_ladder.title: Eliminate Unstated Claims
hint_ladder.text: The passage does not mention salaries or confidentiality.

hint_ladder.title: Choose Summarizing Option
hint_ladder.text: Option B directly captures the relationship between trust, accountability, and transparency.

A.text: Out of scope. Salaries are not mentioned in the passage.

B.text: Correct! Accurately summarizes that accountability and transparency build public trust.

C.text: Directly contradicts the passage's emphasis on transparency.

D.text: False dichotomy. The passage emphasizes both integrity and efficiency equally.

next_time_rule: The main idea must synthesize all key sentences without adding unmentioned assumptions.
blueprint_id: Reading Comprehension — Identifying Main Idea
deconstruct_text:
The passage links public accountability and transaction transparency directly to citizen trust.
Option B synthesizes both sentences accurately.
Option A introduces unmentioned topics (salaries).
Option C contradicts the passage (passage advocates transparency).
Option D creates a false hierarchy between efficiency and integrity.

question_text: The Civil Service Commission issued a MANDATORY directive ordering all agencies to update their personnel records. What is the closest synonym for MANDATORY?

hint_ladder.title: Contextual Clue
hint_ladder.text: The directive requires compliance by all agencies.

hint_ladder.title: Root Meaning
hint_ladder.text: 'Mandatory' comes from mandate — an official command that must be followed.

hint_ladder.title: Eliminate Antonyms
hint_ladder.text: 'Optional' and 'Advisory' mean compliance is voluntary.

hint_ladder.title: Select Synonym
hint_ladder.text: 'Compulsory' means required by law or rule, matching mandatory.

A.text: Direct antonym. Optional means voluntary.

B.text: Correct! Compulsory means required by authority or rule.

C.text: Advisory means offering recommendations, not binding requirements.

D.text: Refers to duration, not obligation.

next_time_rule: Mandatory means compulsory; it requires compliance by law or official command.
blueprint_id: Vocabulary — Synonyms of Administrative Directives
deconstruct_text:
Mandatory means required by law, rule, or authority.
Synonym = Compulsory (obligatory, required).
Antonyms = Optional, Advisory, Discretionary.

question_text: Identify the sentence that avoids a dangling modifier.

options.text: Having completed the audit, the report was submitted to the Bureau of Internal Revenue.
Having completed the audit, the CPA submitted the report to the Bureau of Internal Revenue.
Walking into the office, the computer was left turned on overnight.
While reviewing the documents, a syntax error was discovered by the clerk.

hint_ladder.title: Spot Introductory Phrase
hint_ladder.text: 'Having completed the audit' describes an action performed by a person.

hint_ladder.title: Ask Who Performed Action
hint_ladder.text: Who completed the audit? A report cannot perform an audit!

hint_ladder.title: Check Subject Immediately Following Comma
hint_ladder.text: The noun immediately following the comma MUST be the logical actor.

hint_ladder.title: Select Correct Sentence
hint_ladder.text: In B, 'the CPA' immediately follows the comma, correctly attaching the action.

A.text: Dangling modifier. Implies 'the report' completed the audit.

B.text: Correct! 'The CPA' is the logical subject performing the action 'having completed the audit'.

C.text: Dangling modifier. Implies 'the computer' walked into the office.

D.text: Dangling modifier. Implies 'a syntax error' was reviewing documents.

next_time_rule: Always place the person performing the action immediately after an introductory phrase.
blueprint_id: Dangling Modifiers — Aligning Introductory Participle with Logical Subject
deconstruct_text:
A modifier dangles when the noun it modifies is missing or misplaced.
In A, 'the report' follows the comma -> implies report audited itself!
In B, 'the CPA' correctly follows the comma.
In C, 'the computer' cannot walk into an office.
In D, 'a syntax error' cannot review documents.

question_text: Select the sentence with the correct pronoun case for official communications.

options.text: Between you and I, the regional director will approve the budget proposal.
Between you and me, the regional director will approve the budget proposal.
The division chief awarded the commendation to he and his team.
Him and the auditor inspected the procurement records yesterday.

hint_ladder.title: Identify Preposition
hint_ladder.text: Find the preposition in the introductory phrase.

hint_ladder.title: Recall Preposition Rule
hint_ladder.text: 'Between' is a preposition and takes objective pronouns (me, him, her, us, them).

hint_ladder.title: Test Pronoun Pair
hint_ladder.text: 'Between you and me' uses objective case 'me'.

hint_ladder.title: Confirm Correct Choice
hint_ladder.text: Option B is correct because 'I' is nominative, while 'me' is objective.

A.text: Common hypercorrection. 'I' is nominative; preposition 'between' requires objective 'me'.

B.text: Correct! 'Me' is in objective case following the preposition 'between'.

C.text: Preposition 'to' requires objective pronoun 'him', not nominative 'he'.

D.text: Subject of sentence requires nominative 'He', not objective 'Him'.

next_time_rule: Prepositions (between, to, for, with) always take objective pronouns (me, him, her).
blueprint_id: Pronoun Case — Object of Preposition
deconstruct_text:
Prepositions always require pronouns in the objective case.
'Between' is a preposition -> requires 'you and me' (objective), NOT 'you and I' (nominative).
In C, 'to' takes objective 'him' ('to him and his team').
In D, subject position requires nominative 'He and the auditor'.

question_text: Choose the sentence that adheres to standard Civil Service English grammar rules.

options.text: The committee have decided to postpone the administrative hearing.
Neither the supervisor nor the employees was aware of the memo.
Neither the supervisor nor the employees were aware of the memo.
The list of approved applicants were posted on the bulletin board.

hint_ladder.title: Identify Subject Structure
hint_ladder.text: Look at sentence C with 'Neither... nor...'.

hint_ladder.title: Recall Proximity Rule
hint_ladder.text: When subjects are connected by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees with the closer subject.

hint_ladder.title: Check Subject Agreement
hint_ladder.text: 'employees' (plural) is closer to the verb than 'supervisor' (singular).

hint_ladder.title: Verify Correct Verb Form
hint_ladder.text: Since 'employees' is plural, the plural verb 'were' is correct.

A.text: Collective noun 'committee' acting as a single body requires singular verb 'has decided'.

B.text: Violates proximity rule: 'employees' is plural, so verb must be 'were', not 'was'.

C.text: Correct! The verb 'were' correctly agrees with the nearer plural subject 'employees'.

D.text: Distracted by plural object 'applicants'. Main subject is singular 'list' -> requires 'was'.

next_time_rule: With 'neither/nor', align the verb with the subject closest to it.
blueprint_id: Subject-Verb Agreement — Proximity Rule with Neither/Nor
deconstruct_text:
Rule 1: In 'Neither A nor B' constructions, the verb agrees with subject B (closest subject).
In sentence C, subject B is 'employees' (plural), so 'were' is correct.
In sentence A, collective noun 'committee' acting as a unit requires singular 'has'.
In sentence D, prepositional phrase 'of approved applicants' does not alter the head subject 'list' (singular -> 'was').

question_text: A water reservoir for a barangay can be filled by Pump A in 4 hours and by Pump B in 6 hours. How long will it take to fill the reservoir if both pumps work together?

hint_ladder.title: Find Hourly Work Rates
hint_ladder.text: Pump A fills 1/4 of reservoir per hour. Pump B fills 1/6 per hour.

hint_ladder.title: Invert for Total Time
hint_ladder.text: Total Time = 12 / 5 hours.

hint_ladder.title: Convert to Decimal
hint_ladder.text: 12 / 5 = 2.4 hours (or 2 hours 24 minutes).

B.text: Averaging 4 and 6 to 5 and dividing by 2 (2.5 hrs).

C.text: Averaging 4 and 6 (4+6)/2 = 5 hours.

D.text: Adding 4 + 6 = 10 hours. Two pumps working together take LESS time than one pump alone!

next_time_rule: Work shortcut for 2 workers: Time = (A × B) / (A + B).
blueprint_id: Numerical Ability — Combined Work Formula (1/A + 1/B = 1/T)
deconstruct_text:
Rate A = 1/4 per hour
Rate B = 1/6 per hour
Combined Rate = 1/4 + 1/6 = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12 per hour
Total Time T = 12/5 = 2.4 hours

question_text: A department secretary is currently twice as old as her assistant. Eight years ago, the sum of their ages was 38. How old is the secretary now?

hint_ladder.title: Assign Variables
hint_ladder.text: Let Assistant's age now = x. Then Secretary's age now = 2x.

hint_ladder.title: Express Ages 8 Years Ago
hint_ladder.text: Assistant 8 yrs ago = x - 8. Secretary 8 yrs ago = 2x - 8.

hint_ladder.title: Solve for x and Secretary's Age
hint_ladder.text: 3x = 54 -> x = 18 (Assistant). Secretary = 2x = 36.

A.text: This is the Assistant's age now (18), not the Secretary's age.

B.text: Miscalculating 3x = 48.

C.text: Correct! Assistant = 18, Secretary = 2(18) = 36.

D.text: Adding 8 years to sum instead of subtracting from both.

next_time_rule: Remember to subtract the past years from BOTH people when setting up age equations.
blueprint_id: Numerical Ability — Algebraic Age Problems
deconstruct_text:
Let x = Assistant's age now
Secretary's age now = 2x

8 years ago:
Assistant = x - 8
Secretary = 2x - 8
Sum = (x - 8) + (2x - 8) = 38
3x - 16 = 38
3x = 54 -> x = 18

Secretary's age now = 2 × 18 = 36 years old

question_text: A LGU cooperative deposited ₱50,000 in a government savings account earning 6% simple annual interest. How much total interest will the account earn after 3 years?

hint_ladder.title: Recall Simple Interest Formula
hint_ladder.text: Simple Interest (I) = Principal (P) × Rate (r) × Time (t).

hint_ladder.title: Multiply Principal and Rate
hint_ladder.text: ₱50,000 × 0.06 = ₱3,000 interest per year.

hint_ladder.title: Multiply by Years
hint_ladder.text: ₱3,000 per year × 3 years = ₱9,000.

A.text: Interest for 1 year only (₱50,000 × 0.06 = ₱3,000).

B.text: Interest for 2 years only (₱3,000 × 2).

C.text: Correct! Simple Interest I = 50,000 × 0.06 × 3 = ₱9,000.

D.text: Total balance (Principal + Interest = ₱59,000), not interest earned.

next_time_rule: Simple Interest formula I = P × r × t calculates interest only; add P if total balance is requested.
blueprint_id: Numerical Ability — Simple Interest Formula (I = P r t)

question_text: A municipal health office received a budget increase from ₱800,000 to ₱1,000,000. What was the percentage increase in its budget?

hint_ladder.title: Calculate Amount of Increase
hint_ladder.text: Subtract original budget from new budget: ₱1,000,000 - ₱800,000 = ₱200,000.

hint_ladder.title: Identify Base Value
hint_ladder.text: Percentage increase is always calculated over the ORIGINAL base (₱800,000), not the new amount.

A.text: Divided increase by NEW budget (200,000 / 1,000,000 = 20%). Always divide by ORIGINAL base!

C.text: Rounding 25% up to 30%.

D.text: Comparing original 800k to 1M directly.

next_time_rule: Percentage change formula = (Change / Original Base) × 100.
blueprint_id: Numerical Ability — Percentage Increase
deconstruct_text:
Amount of increase = ₱1,000,000 - ₱800,000 = ₱200,000
Percentage Increase = (Increase / Original Base) × 100
= (200,000 / 800,000) × 100 = (1/4) × 100 = 25%

question_text: An LGU inspection vehicle consumes 18 liters of gasoline to cover a distance of 210 kilometers. How many liters of gasoline will it consume for a 350-kilometer inspection trip?

hint_ladder.title: Identify Direct Relation
hint_ladder.text: More distance = MORE fuel consumed.

hint_ladder.title: Simplify Initial Ratio
hint_ladder.text: 18 / 210 simplifies by dividing by 6 → 3 / 35.

A.text: Calculating 350 ÷ 14.

B.text: Calculating 350 ÷ 12.5.

C.text: Correct! 18 / 210 = 3 / 35. For 350 km, fuel = 3 × 10 = 30 liters.

D.text: Confusing distance 350 with fuel 35 liters.

next_time_rule: Simplify ratios first before cross-multiplying large numbers to make mental calculations much faster.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — vehicle fuel consumption proportion
deconstruct_text:
Direct proportion: 18 / 210 = X / 350
Simplify 18/210:
Divide numerator & denominator by 6 → 3 / 35

Set equal: 3 / 35 = X / 350
Since 350 = 35 × 10:
X = 3 × 10 = 30 liters

question_text: In an agency division, the ratio of permanent staff to casual staff is 4:3, and the ratio of casual staff to job order staff is 6:5. What is the ratio of permanent staff to job order staff?

hint_ladder.title: Identify Common Term
hint_ladder.text: Casual staff is the common term linking Permanent (P:C = 4:3) and Job Order (C:J = 6:5).

hint_ladder.title: Equalize Common Term
hint_ladder.text: In P:C it is 3; in C:J it is 6. LCM of 3 and 6 is 6.

hint_ladder.title: Scale First Ratio
hint_ladder.text: Multiply P:C (4:3) by 2 → P:C becomes 8:6.

hint_ladder.title: Combine and Extract P:J
hint_ladder.text: Now P:C:J = 8:6:5. Therefore, P:J = 8:5.

A.text: Taking the first number 4 and last number 5 directly without equalizing casual staff.

B.text: Correct! Equalizing casual staff to 6 gives P:C:J = 8:6:5, so P:J = 8:5.

C.text: Confusing C:J with P:J.

D.text: Multiplying terms incorrectly (4×3 : 5).

next_time_rule: When connecting two ratios (A:B and B:C), find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the common term B to combine them.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — combining continued ratios (A:B and B:C to find A:C)
deconstruct_text:
Given:
P : C = 4 : 3
C : J = 6 : 5

To combine, make C equal in both ratios:
Multiply P : C by 2 → 8 : 6
C : J is already 6 : 5

Combined ratio P : C : J = 8 : 6 : 5
Therefore, Permanent : Job Order (P : J) = 8 : 5

question_text: A government printer uses 15 reams of paper to produce 600 training manuals. How many reams of paper are required to print 1,000 manuals of the same size?

hint_ladder.title: Identify Direct Proportion
hint_ladder.text: More manuals = MORE paper needed.

hint_ladder.title: Find Reams per Manual
hint_ladder.text: Manuals per ream = 600 ÷ 15 = 40 manuals per ream.

hint_ladder.title: Calculate Reams Needed
hint_ladder.text: 1,000 manuals ÷ 40 manuals/ream = 25 reams.

A.text: Calculating 1,000 ÷ 50.

B.text: Rounding 25 down or miscalculating the ratio.

C.text: Correct! 40 manuals per ream. 1,000 ÷ 40 = 25 reams.

D.text: Dividing 1,000 by 33.3.

next_time_rule: In direct proportion, set up equal ratios (A1/B1 = A2/B2) and cross-multiply to solve for the unknown.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — direct proportion supplies forecasting
deconstruct_text:
Direct proportion: 15 / 600 = X / 1,000
Method 1 (Unit Rate):
600 manuals ÷ 15 reams = 40 manuals per ream
1,000 manuals ÷ 40 = 25 reams

Method 2 (Cross Multiplication):
600X = 15,000 → X = 25 reams

question_text: A ₱90,000 community development grant is divided among three barangays A, B, and C in the ratio 1:2:3. What is the difference in grant amount between Barangay C and Barangay A?

hint_ladder.title: Find Total Parts
hint_ladder.text: Ratio A:B:C = 1:2:3. Total parts = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

hint_ladder.title: Find Ratio Difference
hint_ladder.text: Barangay C has 3 parts, Barangay A has 1 part. Difference = 3 - 1 = 2 parts.

A.text: This is the value of 1 ratio part (Barangay A's share), not the difference.

B.text: Correct! Barangay C (₱45,000) minus Barangay A (₱15,000) = ₱30,000.

C.text: This is Barangay C's total share (3 parts × ₱15,000), not the difference between C and A.

D.text: Adding C and A (3+1 = 4 parts × ₱15,000 = ₱60,000) instead of subtracting.

next_time_rule: To find the difference between two shares, subtract their ratio numbers first, then multiply by the value of one part.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — calculating difference between ratio shares
deconstruct_text:
Total ratio parts = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts
1 part = ₱90,000 ÷ 6 = ₱15,000
Barangay C = 3 × ₱15,000 = ₱45,000
Barangay A = 1 × ₱15,000 = ₱15,000
Difference = ₱45,000 - ₱15,000 = ₱30,000

Shortcut: Difference in parts = 3 - 1 = 2 parts → 2 × ₱15,000 = ₱30,000

question_text: A road maintenance team of 6 DPWH workers can repair a barangay road in 12 days. If 3 additional workers with the same work rate join the team, how many days will it take to finish the repair?

hint_ladder.title: Identify Inverse Proportion
hint_ladder.text: More workers = FEWER days needed to finish the work.

hint_ladder.title: Calculate Total Man-Days
hint_ladder.text: Work = 6 workers × 12 days = 72 man-days.

hint_ladder.title: Find New Worker Count
hint_ladder.text: 6 original + 3 additional = 9 total workers.

hint_ladder.title: Divide Work by New Workers
hint_ladder.text: 72 man-days ÷ 9 workers = 8 days.

A.text: Dividing 12 days by 2.

B.text: Correct! Total work = 72 man-days. 72 man-days ÷ 9 workers = 8 days.

C.text: Subtracting 3 workers directly from 12 days.

D.text: Treating this as direct proportion (6/12 = 9/X → X = 18 days). Remember: more workers = FEWER days!

next_time_rule: For manpower and work time problems, use inverse proportion: (Workers × Days) is constant.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — inverse proportion manpower problems
deconstruct_text:
Inverse proportion rule: W1 × D1 = W2 × D2
Total work = 6 workers × 12 days = 72 man-days
New worker count = 6 + 3 = 9 workers
Days needed = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 days

question_text: On an official LGU land survey map, a scale of 2 centimeters represents an actual distance of 5 kilometers. If two barangay halls are 7 centimeters apart on the map, what is their actual distance in kilometers?

hint_ladder.title: Set Up Proportion
hint_ladder.text: Map (cm) / Actual (km) = 2 / 5 = 7 / X.

hint_ladder.title: Find 1 cm Representation
hint_ladder.text: If 2 cm = 5 km, then 1 cm = 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 km.

hint_ladder.title: Multiply for 7 cm
hint_ladder.text: Actual distance = 7 cm × 2.5 km/cm.

hint_ladder.title: Calculate Value
hint_ladder.text: 7 × 2.5 = 17.5 kilometers.

A.text: Multiplying 7 by 2 instead of 2.5.

B.text: Correct! 1 cm = 2.5 km. 7 cm × 2.5 km/cm = 17.5 km.

C.text: Rounding 17.5 up to 20 or miscalculating 7 × 3.

D.text: Cross-multiplying 7 × 5 = 35 without dividing by 2.

next_time_rule: In map scale problems, find what 1 unit on the map represents in real life first, then multiply.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — map scale proportional reasoning
deconstruct_text:
Scale: 2 cm = 5 km → 1 cm = 2.5 km
Map distance = 7 cm
Actual distance = 7 × 2.5 = 17.5 km

Alternatively, cross-multiply:
2 / 5 = 7 / X → 2X = 35 → X = 17.5 km

question_text: A Provincial Capitol purchased 48 desktop computers and 32 printers for its field offices. Express the ratio of computers to printers in simplest form.

hint_ladder.title: Write Initial Ratio
hint_ladder.text: Computers : Printers = 48 : 32.

hint_ladder.title: Find Great Common Divisor
hint_ladder.text: What is the largest number that divides both 48 and 32?

hint_ladder.title: Divide by GCD
hint_ladder.text: Greatest Common Divisor is 16.

A.text: Dividing 48 by 12 and 32 by 8 (inconsistent divisor).

B.text: Correct! Dividing both 48 and 32 by their GCD (16) yields 3:2.

C.text: Reversing the terms (Printers to Computers ratio 2:3 instead of Computers to Printers).

D.text: Dividing by 8 gives 6:4, but 6:4 can still be reduced further to 3:2.

next_time_rule: Always divide ratio terms by their Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) until they cannot be simplified further.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — simplifying ratios into lowest terms
deconstruct_text:
Computers = 48, Printers = 32
Ratio = 48 : 32
Divide both terms by 16:
48 ÷ 16 = 3
32 ÷ 16 = 2
Simplest ratio = 3:2

question_text: A disaster relief fund of ₱120,000 is allocated to three barangays in proportion to their population ratio of 3:4:5. How much budget will the barangay with the smallest population receive?

hint_ladder.title: Sum the Ratio
hint_ladder.text: Total parts = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.

hint_ladder.title: Smallest Barangay Share
hint_ladder.text: Smallest ratio = 3 parts.

B.text: This is the middle barangay share (4 parts × ₱10,000 = ₱40,000).

C.text: This is the largest barangay share (5 parts × ₱10,000 = ₱50,000).

D.text: Dividing ₱120,000 by 2.

next_time_rule: Always check whether the question asks for the smallest, largest, or specific ratio part before picking your answer.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — dividing budget by population ratio
deconstruct_text:
Ratio = 3 : 4 : 5
Total parts = 12
Value per part = ₱120,000 ÷ 12 = ₱10,000
Smallest share (3 parts) = 3 × ₱10,000 = ₱30,000

question_text: In a municipal health center, the ratio of registered nurses to medical technologists is 5:2. If there are 35 registered nurses, how many medical technologists are employed?

hint_ladder.title: Identify Given Values
hint_ladder.text: Ratio of Nurses : MedTechs is 5 : 2.

hint_ladder.title: Find the Multiplier
hint_ladder.text: If 5 parts = 35 nurses, how much is 1 part?

hint_ladder.title: Calculate One Part
hint_ladder.text: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 nurses per part.

hint_ladder.title: Final Multiply
hint_ladder.text: MedTechs = 2 parts × 7 = 14.

A.text: Dividing 35 by 3.5 or miscalculating 5 × 2.

B.text: Correct! 5 parts = 35, so 1 part = 7. MedTechs = 2 parts × 7 = 14.

C.text: Subtracting 20 from 35 instead of using ratio proportion.

D.text: Calculating 35 minus 15.

next_time_rule: In direct proportion ratios (A:B = Given:X), divide the given quantity by its corresponding ratio number to find the multiplier.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — finding unknown quantity in direct proportion
deconstruct_text:
Nurses : MedTechs = 5 : 2
5 parts = 35 nurses → 1 part = 35 ÷ 5 = 7
MedTechs = 2 parts = 2 × 7 = 14

question_text: A government office distributed ₱45,000 among three employees in the ratio 2:3:4. How much did the employee with the largest share receive?

hint_ladder.title: See the Pattern
hint_ladder.text: This is a ratio problem — you need to divide a total into parts.

hint_ladder.title: Strip the Noise
hint_ladder.text: Add the ratio parts: 2+3+4 = 9 total parts.

hint_ladder.title: Eliminate One
hint_ladder.text: ₱45,000 ÷ 9 = ₱5,000 per part. The largest share is 4 parts.

hint_ladder.title: Almost There
hint_ladder.text: 4 × ₱5,000 = ₱20,000. Look for this value.

A.text: This is the middle share (3 parts × ₱5,000 = ₱15,000), not the largest.

B.text: Dividing by an incorrect number of parts. Always use the total ratio parts.

C.text: Correct! 4 parts × ₱5,000 = ₱20,000.

D.text: Dividing ₱45,000 by 2 (smallest ratio). Divide by TOTAL parts (9), not individual.

next_time_rule: Whenever you see a ratio, add up ALL parts first before dividing.
blueprint_id: Ratio and Proportion — dividing a total amount into parts based on a given ratio
deconstruct_text:
Step 1: Add ratio parts → 2+3+4 = 9 total parts
Step 2: Find value of one part → ₱45,000 ÷ 9 = ₱5,000
Step 3: Largest share = 4 × ₱5,000 = ₱20,000

question_text:
Arrange the following government employee names in correct alphabetical filing order:
1. De la Cruz, Juan
2. Del Rosario, Maria
3. De Castro, Ana
4. De Leon, Pedro

hint_ladder.title: Recall Filing Rules for Prefixes
hint_ladder.text: Foreign prefixes (De, De la, Del) are filed as a single unit or letter by letter.

hint_ladder.title: Compare First Letters
hint_ladder.text: De Castro (De C...), De la Cruz (De l...), De Leon (De L...), Del Rosario (Del R...).

hint_ladder.title: Sort Letter by Letter
hint_ladder.text: De C... comes first (3), then De l... (1), then De L... (4), then Del R... (2).

hint_ladder.title: Select Correct Sequence
hint_ladder.text: Sequence is 3, 1, 4, 2.

A.text: Correct! Alphabetical order letter by letter: De Castro (3), De la Cruz (1), De Leon (4), Del Rosario (2).

B.text: Unsorted sequence as presented.

C.text: Swapping De la Cruz and De Leon.

D.text: Placing Del Rosario first.

next_time_rule: File names with prefixes (De, De la, Del) letter by letter from left to right.
blueprint_id: Alphabetical Filing — Prefix Surnames (De, De la, Del)

Standard Filing Rules treat prefixes letter-by-letter:
1. De Castro, Ana (D-E-C...) -> #3
2. De la Cruz, Juan (D-E-L-A-C...) -> #1
3. De Leon, Pedro (D-E-L-E...) -> #4
4. Del Rosario, Maria (D-E-L-R...) -> #2
Order: 3, 1, 4, 2.

question_text: According to Article II Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution, the Philippines is a democratic and republican State. Where does sovereignty reside?

options.text: Sovereignty resides in the President of the Philippines.
Sovereignty resides in the Supreme Court.
Sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them.
Sovereignty resides in the Armed Forces of the Philippines.

hint_ladder.text: Article II outlines Declaration of Principles and State Policies.

hint_ladder.title: Recall Section 1 Text
hint_ladder.text: Section 1 defines the democratic nature of the Republic.

hint_ladder.title: Source of Authority
hint_ladder.text: All government authority emanates from the citizens.

hint_ladder.title: Select Option C
hint_ladder.text: Option C is 'Sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them.'

A.text: The President is an elected servant of the people, not the seat of sovereignty.

B.text: The Judiciary interprets law, but sovereignty belongs to the people.

C.text: Correct! Article II Section 1 states sovereignty resides in the people.

D.text: Article II Section 3 states military is protector of people, not sovereign.

next_time_rule: Article II Section 1 states that sovereignty resides in the people and all authority emanates from them.

1987 Constitution Article II Section 1:

question_text:
Rule: 'An applicant is granted an interview ONLY IF they pass the written examination and possess a bachelor's degree.'
Fact: Jose passed the written examination but does not possess a bachelor's degree.
Conclusion: Is Jose eligible for an interview?

options.text: Yes, because passing the written exam is sufficient.
No, because both conditions must be satisfied.
Yes, if he submits an extension request.
Cannot be determined from the rule.

hint_ladder.title: Analyze 'ONLY IF' Condition
hint_ladder.text: 'ONLY IF' introduces necessary conditions. BOTH conditions are required.

hint_ladder.title: Check Requirements
hint_ladder.text: Requirement 1: Pass written exam. Requirement 2: Bachelor's degree.

hint_ladder.title: Evaluate Jose's Status
hint_ladder.text: Jose has Requirement 1, but lacks Requirement 2.

hint_ladder.title: Deduce Eligibility
hint_ladder.text: Failing one necessary condition makes Jose ineligible (No).

A.text: Treats a necessary condition as sufficient.

B.text: Correct! 'ONLY IF' requires BOTH conditions to be true.

C.text: Speculative exception not mentioned in the rule.

D.text: Incorrect. The rule strictly determines eligibility.

next_time_rule: In 'ONLY IF' rules, ALL listed conditions must be met for eligibility.
blueprint_id: Logical Reasoning — Necessary vs Sufficient Conditions
deconstruct_text:
'ONLY IF' establishes necessary conditions.
Interview -> Pass Exam AND Bachelor's Degree.
Since Jose lacks a bachelor's degree, the necessary condition is false.
Therefore, Jose is NOT eligible for an interview.

question_text: Find the next number in the series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, __?

hint_ladder.title: Identify Pattern in Differences
hint_ladder.text: The differences are doubling: +4, +8, +16, +32.

hint_ladder.title: Find Next Difference
hint_ladder.text: Next difference is 32 × 2 = +64.

A.text: Adding 32 twice instead of doubling the difference to 64.

B.text: Correct! Pattern doubles differences (+64) or applies (2n + 1) -> 127.

C.text: Confusing (2n + 1) with pure power of 2 (2^7 = 128).

D.text: Adding 72 instead of 64.

next_time_rule: Check both difference growth (+4, +8, +16) and multiplier rules (×2 + 1) when solving number series.

question_text:
Premise 1: All department heads are career service eligible.
Premise 2: Maria is a department head.
Which conclusion logically follows?

options.text: Maria is not career service eligible.
All career service eligibles are department heads.
Maria will be promoted next year.

hint_ladder.title: Identify Set Inclusion
hint_ladder.text: Department heads belong inside the set of Career Service Eligibles.

hint_ladder.title: Place Individual in Set
hint_ladder.text: Maria is placed inside the Department Heads set.

hint_ladder.title: Deduce Property
hint_ladder.text: Since Maria is in Department Heads, she MUST also be in Career Service Eligibles.

hint_ladder.title: Select Matching Conclusion
hint_ladder.text: Option B is a valid direct deduction.

A.text: Direct contradiction of the premises.

B.text: Correct! Valid deductive conclusion (Modus Ponens).

C.text: Converse fallacy. Saying All A are B does not mean All B are A.

D.text: Speculative assumption not contained in premises.

next_time_rule: If All A are B and X is A, then X is definitely B (do not flip the direction).
blueprint_id: Logical Reasoning — Categorical Syllogism (Modus Ponens)
deconstruct_text:
Classic Modus Ponens:
All A are B.
X is A.
Therefore, X is B.
Here A = Department Heads, B = Career Service Eligible, X = Maria.
Maria MUST be career service eligible.
